FLASHCARD SET · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Science, Nature & Discovery flashcards.

Thirty-five big science ideas, one card each: ants, bees, magnets, rain, shadows, volcanoes. Show the card, wonder out loud together, then try the little experiment — science at four is talking, watching and testing, not memorising.

These cards belong to Class 31 · Science, Nature & Discovery on the Kiddo School learning path.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Each card has its own page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Tap any card to open it.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Ask the question on the card

    Every card answers one small question — where does rain come from? what does a magnet stick to? Read the question, guess together FIRST, then turn the card over and talk about the answer. The guess matters more than being right.

  2. 02

    Name what you both see

    Look at the picture and say what you notice: the ant is carrying, the shadow is long, the ice is dripping. Naming details is exactly what young scientists do — observation comes before explanation.

  3. 03

    Try the little experiment

    Each card page has a hands-on idea — an ant trail to watch, a magnet hunt, an ice cube on the windowsill. Two minutes with the real thing beats ten with the card; the card is the invitation.

  4. 04

    Let one card lead a whole day

    Pick the weather you actually have, the bug you actually saw, the fruit you actually ate. One card, talked about at breakfast and spotted outside at noon, is a full science lesson.

      Ant Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ants are tiny team workers: one ant finds food, tells the others, and a whole line shows up to help carry it home.

      What this card opens up

      Names the tiny hauler that carries crumbs ten times its own size.

      Try it for real

      Follow one ant on the pavement and count the turns it takes.

      What kids learn from it

      Insects work in teams; small legs do big jobs.

      Print tips

      A4 is fine — this one lives on the picnic table.

      A question to ask

      Watch, never touch: ants bite when their line is blocked.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Ant lesson on the Learning Path.

      Bee Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Bees visit flowers to drink sweet nectar — and carry pollen from flower to flower, which is how plants make seeds and fruit.

      What this card opens up

      Introduces the striped visitor every flower was waiting for.

      Try it for real

      Buzz and land on five cushion "flowers" before the count ends.

      What kids learn from it

      Bees carry pollen between flowers, which makes fruit grow.

      Print tips

      Cardstock; keep it for calm garden bee days.

      A question to ask

      Statue-still bodies get calm bees — practise in the garden.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Bee lesson on the Learning Path.

      Dinosaur Fossil Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Fossils are the stone-hard remains of living things from long ago: buried fast, pressed by layers, and turned to rock over millions of years — that is how we know dinosaurs at all.

      Try it for real

      What kids learn from it

      Fossils are pressed remains from very long ago.

      Print tips

      Museum-visit warm-up material.

      A question to ask

      Bury it in the flour bin for a second dig.

      What Magnets Attract Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Magnets pull — but only some things: iron and steel stick, wood, plastic, glass and paper do not. Testing what sticks is real experimenting.

      What this card opens up

      Proves the invisible pull with one card and one magnet.

      Try it for real

      Magnet fishing: paperclips out of a bowl on a string — count the catch.

      What kids learn from it

      Magnets pull some metals and skip others.

      Print tips

      Next to the magnet tin.

      A question to ask

      Predict first — fridge, spoons, coins — then check.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the What Magnets Attract lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Science, Nature & Discovery (Class 31) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SCIENCE, NATURE & DISCOVERY · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Magnet Force Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A magnet can move things without touching them: it pulls steel from a distance, pulls hardest at its ends — the poles — and pushes another magnet away when like poles meet.

      What this card opens up

      Names the trick that looks like magic and is actually science.

      Try it for real

      Paper maze: drag a paperclip through from underneath, hand unseen.

      What kids learn from it

      The pull works through paper, air and sometimes tables.

      Print tips

      Cardstock — it holds still during maze runs.

      A question to ask

      Two magnets pushing apart beats any toy that day.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Magnet Force lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Science, Nature & Discovery (Class 31) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SCIENCE, NATURE & DISCOVERY · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Sound Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Every sound is a shaking: the drum skin wobbles, the air carries the wobble to your ear, and your eardrum wobbles too — that is hearing.

      What this card opens up

      Shows what ears catch: shaking air, arriving late and quiet.

      Try it for real

      Two cups and string: whisper across the room and hear it arrive.

      What kids learn from it

      Sounds travel in waves; big hits make big sounds.

      Print tips

      Lives in the listening corner.

      A question to ask

      Bang a pan far away, then near — same pan, new sound.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Sound lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Science, Nature & Discovery (Class 31) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · SCIENCE, NATURE & DISCOVERY · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Shadow Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A shadow is the dark shape where something blocks the light: your body stops the sunshine, and the dark patch on the ground is the shape of the stopping.

      What this card opens up

      The dark copy that follows every sunny walk, explained.

      Try it for real

      Shadow tag in the yard: step on each other's shadows.

      What kids learn from it

      Any dark patch shaped exactly like whatever stopped the light.

      Print tips

      Chalk-shadow days want the stiff version.

      A question to ask

      Long shadows at teatime, short at noon — measure with a shoe.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Shadow lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Science, Nature & Discovery (Class 31) class on the Learning Path.

      Feather Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Feathers are a bird’s all-in-one gear: flight feathers catch the air for flying, and soft fluffy down holds warm air close like a duvet.

      What this card opens up

      Describes the fluffiest flying tool in the garden.

      Try it for real

      Feather race: blow it across the table, no hands, edge wins.

      What kids learn from it

      Feathers are light, strong and water-shrugging.

      Print tips

      Beside the nature-finds tray.

      A question to ask

      Found feathers go in the nature box — wash hands after.

      Teach it, step by step
